The structure of DNA was discovered in 1953 by James Watson and Francis Crick. Using data from X-ray diffraction by Rosalind Franklin, they unveiled the famous double helix model. This discovery unlocked the fundamental building blocks of life.
    Understanding DNA has revolutionised biology, medicine, and forensics. It has led to advances in genetic engineering, disease detection, and personalised medicine. The discovery remains one of the most important scientific breakthroughs of the 20th century.

advanced.text:
The Taj Mahal in India is widely considered the most beautiful building in the world. It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. This magnificent mausoleum combines Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural styles.
    The white marble structure is famous for its stunning symmetry and intricate carvings. It attracts millions of visitors each year and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Taj Mahal stands as an enduring symbol of love and artistic perfection.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Vikings, known for their seafaring skills, were much more than fierce raiders. They were also skilled traders, explorers, and craftspeople who travelled as far as North America. Their longships were masterpieces of naval engineering that could cross vast oceans.
    The Vikings had a rich mythology and a complex social structure. They left a lasting legacy on European history, including place names and democratic traditions. Their adventurous spirit continues to capture the imagination of people today.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Silk Road was a vast network of trade routes connecting Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. It was not a single road but a complex web of overland and maritime paths. Goods like silk, spices, and precious metals were exchanged, but so were ideas, religions, and technologies.
    The Silk Road facilitated the spread of Buddhism, Islam, and Christianity across continents. It also enabled the transmission of papermaking and the compass from China to the West. This exchange shaped the course of world history in profound ways.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Northern Lights, or Aurora Borealis, are one of nature's most spectacular displays. These colourful lights dance across the sky in polar regions, created by solar particles colliding with the Earth's magnetic field. They can appear as ribbons, spirals, or curtains of green, red, and purple.
    The phenomenon has inspired countless myths and legends throughout history. People from all over the world travel to countries like Norway, Canada, and Iceland to witness this breathtaking sight. It is a reminder of the beauty and power of the natural world.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The ancient city of Petra in Jordan is one of the most remarkable archaeological sites in the world. Carved into rose-coloured cliffs by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago, it is famous for its intricate rock-cut architecture. The most iconic structure is the Treasury, which appears at the end of a narrow canyon.
    Petra was a bustling trading hub that controlled key trade routes. After centuries of abandonment, it was rediscovered in the 19th century. Today, it stands as a testament to human ingenuity and is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
Albert Einstein was one of the most brilliant minds in human history. His theory of relativity revolutionised our understanding of space, time, and gravity. He showed that time is not absolute but can slow down or speed up depending on gravity and speed.
    Einstein also contributed to the development of quantum mechanics and wrote the famous equation E=mc². He was known for his humility and his commitment to peace. His ideas continue to shape modern physics and cosmology.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Ottoman Empire, at its height, controlled vast territories across Europe, Asia, and Africa. It lasted over 600 years and was one of the most powerful empires in history. The empire was known for its cultural and artistic achievements, from architecture to calligraphy.
    The Ottomans also developed a sophisticated legal and administrative system. Their empire eventually collapsed after World War I, giving rise to the modern Republic of Turkey. The legacy of the Ottomans remains visible in the cultures of many countries.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
Mount Everest, standing at 29,032 feet, is the highest mountain on Earth. Located in the Himalayas on the border of Nepal and Tibet, it has been a powerful symbol of human endurance and ambition. Climbing Everest requires months of preparation and is extremely dangerous.
    Since Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay first summited in 1953, over 5,000 people have followed in their footsteps. Many have lost their lives on its icy slopes, making it both a triumph and a tragedy. Everest continues to inspire explorers and mountaineers from all over the world.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Rosetta Stone was the key to deciphering ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs. Discovered in 1799, this granodiorite stone contained the same text in three scripts: hieroglyphic, demotic, and Greek. Scholars were finally able to decode the mysterious writing system.
    The stone was found by French soldiers during Napoleon's campaign and later became British property. It is now one of the most popular exhibits at the British Museum. The Rosetta Stone gave us access to a vast history that was previously impossible to read.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Galapagos Islands are home to some of the most unique species on Earth. Their isolation led to the evolution of fascinating creatures, like giant tortoises and marine iguanas. These islands played a crucial role in Charles Darwin's development of his theory of evolution by natural selection.
    Darwin's observations in the Galapagos changed the way we understand the history of life. The islands remain a living laboratory for scientists and a sanctuary for biodiversity. They are a testament to the power of nature to create diversity.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The invention of the internet has transformed nearly every aspect of modern life. It began as a military project called ARPANET in the 1960s and evolved into the global network we know today. The internet enables instant communication and access to unlimited information.
    It has revolutionised fields like education, healthcare, and commerce. However, it has also brought challenges like cybersecurity threats and information overload. The internet's future will depend on how we manage its impact on society.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa. It is an immense expanse of sand dunes, rocky plateaus, and extreme temperatures. Despite its harsh environment, the Sahara has supported human life for thousands of years.
    Ancient trade routes crossed this vast desert, connecting sub-Saharan Africa with the Mediterranean world. Today, the Sahara is both a challenge and a wonder, attracting adventurers and scientists alike. Its landscapes are breathtaking and unforgiving.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Aztecs built a vast empire in central Mexico before the Spanish conquest. Their capital, Tenochtitlán, was one of the largest cities in the world at that time. The Aztecs were skilled engineers who built floating gardens and magnificent temples.
    Their society was highly structured, with a powerful ruler and a complex religious system. They also made significant contributions to mathematics and astronomy. The arrival of the Spanish in 1519 led to the empire's rapid collapse.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The aurora australis, or Southern Lights, is the southern counterpart of the aurora borealis. It is visible from places like Antarctica, New Zealand, and southern Australia. This natural phenomenon is just as spectacular, with waves of colour that illuminate the night sky.
    The lights are caused by the same solar activity that creates the Northern Lights. They have inspired local myths and legends for generations. Seeing the Southern Lights is a dream for many travellers.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Hubble Space Telescope has transformed our understanding of the universe. Launched in 1990, it has provided breathtaking images of distant galaxies, nebulas, and planets. These images have revealed the immense scale and beauty of the cosmos.
    Hubble has also helped scientists measure the rate of expansion of the universe. It has made discoveries that have rewritten astronomy textbooks. The telescope continues to operate and is one of NASA's most successful missions.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Underground Railroad was a secret network of routes and safe houses. It helped enslaved African Americans escape to freedom in the 19th century. It was not a physical railroad but a system of courageous individuals who risked their lives.
    Leaders like Harriet Tubman guided hundreds of people to safety. This movement represented a powerful act of resistance against slavery. It remains a powerful symbol of courage and the fight for human rights.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Panama Canal is one of the greatest engineering feats of the modern age. Connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, it drastically shortened maritime trade routes. The canal was completed in 1914 after decades of work and thousands of workers' lives.
    Its construction involved overcoming tropical diseases and difficult terrain. The canal has been crucial for global shipping and continues to be a vital passage. It remains a symbol of human ambition and perseverance.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Vikings explored and settled in Iceland around the 9th century. They were drawn by its natural resources and opportunities for farming. Iceland's dramatic landscape of volcanoes, glaciers, and waterfalls must have been both intimidating and awe-inspiring.
    The settlers established a unique society with a famous parliament, the Althing, which is one of the world's oldest. Their sagas, written in Old Norse, continue to be studied today. Iceland's history is deeply rooted in Norse culture and tradition.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Caspian Sea is actually the largest lake in the world by area. It is bounded by five countries, including Russia and Iran. The sea is rich in natural resources, particularly oil and natural gas.
    Its ecosystem is unique, with species found nowhere else on Earth. The region has been a crossroads for trade and culture for centuries. The future of the Caspian Sea is closely tied to international politics.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 1,400 miles off Australia's coast. It is home to thousands of marine species, including fish, turtles, and sharks. The reef is a natural wonder and a vital part of the ocean's ecosystem.
    However, climate change and ocean acidification are causing coral bleaching and threatening its survival. Scientists are working hard to protect this incredible ecosystem. The reef's future is uncertain, but efforts to preserve it are intensifying.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Inca Empire was the largest empire in pre-Columbian America, stretching from Ecuador to Chile. They built an extensive network of roads and bridges across the Andes Mountains. Their capital, Cusco, was a centre of political and religious power.
    The Incas are famous for their agricultural innovations and stonework, including the site of Machu Picchu. Their empire was conquered by the Spanish in the 16th century. Inca culture and traditions still survive in the Andean regions today.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The development of photography in the 19th century changed how we see the world. It allowed people to document history, culture, and everyday life in new ways. Early cameras required long exposures and heavy equipment, but they captured images that drawings could not.
    Photography has become an essential tool in journalism, science, and personal expression. It has given us a visual record of events and places. The evolution of this medium continues to influence modern society.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Suez Canal is a vital waterway that connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. It was completed in 1869 and dramatically shortened the shipping route between Europe and Asia. The canal is a crucial economic lifeline for Egypt and global trade.
    Its construction involved immense effort and was a major engineering project. The Suez Canal has been a point of international conflict throughout its history. It remains one of the world's most strategically important waterways.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Bering Strait is a narrow passage between Asia and North America. It has been a vital link for human migration and trade. The strait is only about 55 miles wide, but it is often frozen, creating a land bridge that was used in ancient times.
    This region is home to diverse indigenous cultures with deep historical ties. The political boundary between Russia and the United States runs through the strait. It is a place of both ecological and historical significance.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Polynesians were master navigators who explored and settled vast areas of the Pacific Ocean. They used stars, currents, and the behaviour of birds to find their way across thousands of miles. Their voyages were remarkable, considering they did not have modern navigational tools.
    They inhabited islands across the Pacific, creating a rich cultural heritage. The great migrations and settlement of places like Hawaii and New Zealand are still celebrated. Polynesian navigation remains a powerful symbol of human exploration.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The invention of the telephone by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876 revolutionised communication. It allowed people to speak to each other over long distances in real time. This invention laid the foundation for the development of modern telecommunications.
    Bell's work opened the door to a world where voice communication became instantaneous. Today, the telephone has evolved into the smartphone, a powerful tool. This invention changed the way we connect with each other forever.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The ancient city of Babylon was one of the most famous cities of antiquity. It was the capital of the Babylonian Empire and was known for its magnificent architecture. The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
    Babylon was a centre of learning, mathematics, and astronomy. Its remains lie in modern-day Iraq, a testament to its former glory. The city's legacy continues to influence our culture and imagination.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The moon has always been a source of human wonder and inspiration. It is Earth's only natural satellite and has been studied for centuries. The moon's gravitational pull is responsible for the ocean tides on Earth.
    The Apollo missions in the 1960s and 1970s brought humans to its surface for the first time. Those missions gave us a new perspective on our place in the universe. The moon continues to be a target for scientific exploration and discovery.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Australian outback is a vast and remote region in the interior of Australia. It is characterised by red deserts, rugged mountains, and sparse vegetation. The outback has a unique beauty and is home to a variety of wildlife.
    Indigenous Australian cultures have thrived in this harsh environment for tens of thousands of years. It is a place of great spiritual significance and natural wonder. The outback remains one of the most untouched places on Earth.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The human brain is one of the most complex organs in the known universe. It is responsible for all thought, memory, emotion, and movement. The brain weighs only about three pounds but contains billions of nerve cells.
    Neuroscience is continuously uncovering new secrets about how the brain works. Understanding the brain is key to treating conditions like Alzheimer's and mental illness. The future of medicine will rely heavily on brain research.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash. This catastrophic event preserved these cities for future generations. The remains provide a unique snapshot of daily life in ancient Rome.
    The site is one of the most important archaeological discoveries in history. It offers valuable information about Roman society, art, and architecture. Pompeii remains a popular and important site for visitors and researchers.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The South Pole is the southernmost point on Earth and one of the coldest places. It is located in Antarctica, a vast and icy continent. The conditions are extreme, with winter temperatures dropping below -70°C.
    The South Pole has been a site of scientific research since the early 20th century. It is home to the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station. The region is also important for climate research and studies of the Earth's atmosphere.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The development of the steam engine was a key driver of the Industrial Revolution. It allowed factories to be built away from water sources and increased production. The steam engine revolutionised transportation, enabling the development of steamships and railways.
    This technology changed the economic and social landscape of the world. It made it possible to travel and trade on an unprecedented scale. The steam engine's invention marked the start of a new era in human history.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The art of mosaics involves creating images using small pieces of coloured glass, stone, or ceramic. This ancient art form has been used for thousands of years to decorate walls, floors, and ceilings. Mosaics were particularly popular in the Roman and Byzantine empires.
    The intricate designs and skilled craftsmanship are still admired today. Mosaics provide valuable insights into historical artistic techniques. This art form continues to be used in both traditional and modern contexts.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The invention of the compass revolutionised navigation and exploration. This simple device, which uses a magnet to point north, allowed sailors to venture far from land. The compass was crucial for the Age of Discovery and the global trade that followed.
    Without the compass, many of the great voyages of history would have been impossible. It opened up the world to exploration and trade. The compass remains one of the most important inventions in history.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Sami people are the indigenous inhabitants of the Arctic region of Europe. They have lived in northern Scandinavia and Russia for thousands of years. Their culture is closely connected to reindeer herding, which has been a central part of their way of life.
    The Sami have their own languages and a rich tradition of storytelling and music. Today, they face challenges related to climate change and modernisation. Their culture and rights are increasingly being recognised internationally.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Mediterranean Sea is a cradle of civilisation, surrounded by Europe, Africa, and Asia. Its shores have been home to ancient cultures like the Greeks, Romans, and Egyptians. The sea facilitated trade, cultural exchange, and conflict throughout history.
    The Mediterranean is a melting pot of cultures, religions, and languages. Its beauty and historical significance attract millions of tourists each year. The sea remains a vital part of the global economy and cultural heritage.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Dead Sea is a salt lake located between Israel and Jordan. It is famous for its extremely high salt content, which makes it impossible for fish to live in it. People can easily float in its waters due to the buoyancy created by the salt.
    The unique mineral-rich mud from the Dead Sea is used in cosmetics and treatments. The area is also historically significant, being near several important sites. It is a place of natural beauty and historical importance.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Gobi Desert is a vast desert in northern China and southern Mongolia. It has a unique ecosystem with diverse wildlife, including camels and snow leopards. The Gobi Desert is notable for its harsh climate and dramatic landscapes.
    Fossil discoveries in the desert have provided insight into prehistoric life. The region is also historically significant as it was part of the Mongol Empire. Today, the Gobi Desert is an important site for both research and tourism.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Great Sphinx of Giza is an ancient statue that has fascinated people for centuries. It is a massive limestone structure with the body of a lion and the head of a human. The statue is located near the Great Pyramids of Giza in Egypt.
    The identity of the Pharaoh depicted by the Sphinx remains a topic of debate. It has suffered from erosion over thousands of years but has been restored several times. The Sphinx remains one of Egypt's most enduring and mysterious symbols.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Amazon River is the second longest river in the world and is located in South America. It flows through the Amazon Rainforest, carrying more water than any other river. The river is home to diverse aquatic life, including the piranha and the pink river dolphin.
    The Amazon River has been a critical route for exploration and trade. Its basin is home to many indigenous communities. The future of the river and its rainforest is closely linked to environmental protection.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Moai statues of Easter Island are some of the most mysterious sculptures in the world. Carved from volcanic rock, they are enormous, weighing many tons. The statues are thought to represent the ancestors of the islanders, who lived on the island.
    Their transportation and placement remain a topic of debate. The construction of these statues contributed to deforestation and resource depletion on the island. They stand as a powerful symbol of both human achievement and environmental fragility.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Persians were a powerful and influential civilisation that built a vast empire. Their empire, founded by Cyrus the Great, stretched from the Mediterranean to India. The Persians were known for their administrative efficiency and cultural diversity.
    They also made significant contributions to art, architecture, and the management of water resources. The empire fell to Alexander the Great in the 4th century BC. Persian culture has deeply influenced the history of the Middle East.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Chernobyl disaster of 1986 was one of the worst nuclear accidents in history. It occurred at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine. The explosion released large amounts of radioactive material into the atmosphere.
    The area around the plant became a highly contaminated exclusion zone. The disaster had a devastating impact on human health and the environment. Chernobyl serves as a stark warning about the dangers of nuclear power.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The first successful ascent of Mount Everest was made by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay. Their achievement in 1953 captured the world's imagination. It was a testament to human endurance and teamwork.
    Their ascent opened the mountain to future climbers and explorers. Mount Everest has since become a symbol of adventure and human potential. The legacy of this first ascent continues to inspire mountaineers worldwide.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Great Pyramids of Giza are one of the most iconic structures in the world. They were built as tombs for the Egyptian Pharaohs, including Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure. These structures have stood for over 4,500 years, a testament to the skill of ancient builders.
    They were originally covered in polished limestone, which reflected the sun's light. The Pyramids remain a symbol of Egypt's ancient glory and are a popular tourist destination. They are one of the most visited landmarks in the world.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Victoria Falls, located on the Zambezi River, is one of the largest and most spectacular waterfalls in the world. It is over a mile wide and plunges into a deep gorge. The falls are a major tourist attraction and are known as the 'Smoke that Thunders'.
    They were discovered by Europeans in the 19th century and named after Queen Victoria. The falls are a source of power and a vital part of the region's ecosystem. They also hold significant cultural and spiritual importance for local communities.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The Balkan Peninsula is a region of Europe known for its mountainous terrain and complex history. It has been a crossroads of civilisations, with influences from Greece, Rome, and the Ottoman Empire. The region has experienced many conflicts and political changes throughout its history.
    The Balkans are home to diverse cultures, languages, and religions. They also have stunning natural beauty, from the Adriatic coast to the Dinaric Alps. The region remains a fascinating and dynamic part of Europe.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The first successful heart transplant was performed by Dr. Christiaan Barnard in 1967. The operation, which took place in South Africa, was a medical milestone. It demonstrated the possibility of replacing a diseased heart with a healthy one.
    The surgery was fraught with medical and ethical challenges. It opened the door to advances in organ transplantation and surgical techniques. The procedure has saved many lives and remains a beacon of hope for patients with heart disease.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The history of tea stretches back thousands of years, originating in China. It became a significant part of Asian culture and later spread to the West. Tea was introduced to Europe in the 17th century and became a popular beverage.
    The British developed a culture of tea drinking that became central to their identity. Tea is now the second most consumed drink in the world. Its rich history and global influence make it a fascinating subject.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The city of Rome is famously known as the 'Eternal City' because of its long history and cultural significance. It was the centre of the Roman Empire and remains a repository of art, architecture, and history. The city is home to the Vatican, a city-state and the centre of the Catholic Church.
    Rome's ancient ruins, including the Colosseum and the Roman Forum, attract millions of tourists. The city is a living museum, blending ancient history with modern life. It continues to fascinate and inspire people from all over the world.

advanced.instruction: Запишите голосовое сообщение, прочитав весь текст вслух четко и разборчиво.
advanced.text:
The history of chocolate begins with the ancient Mesoamericans, who cultivated the cacao tree. They considered chocolate a sacred drink, used in religious ceremonies. Chocolate was introduced to Europe by Spanish explorers, who sweetened it with sugar.
    It soon became a popular delicacy throughout Europe and eventually the world. Today, chocolate is a beloved treat available in countless forms. Its journey from a sacred drink to a global commodity is truly remarkable.

    The Stone Age was a crucial phase in human evolution, laying the foundations for civilisation. It witnessed the transition from a nomadic lifestyle to settled farming communities. This period set the stage for the rise of complex societies.

    The Berbers are known for their vibrant art, music, and architecture. They continue to play a vital role in the social and political landscape of North Africa. Their heritage is an integral part of the region's identity.

    It is capable of producing a wide range of dynamics and emotions. The piano has been used by countless famous composers, from Mozart to Rachmaninoff. Its versatility and expressive power make it one of the most beloved instruments.

The Voynich Manuscript is a mysterious and ancient book that has puzzled scholars for centuries. It is written in an unknown script and is filled with strange illustrations of plants and astronomical charts. The manuscript has never been deciphered, and its origin remains a mystery.
    The author and purpose of the Voynich Manuscript are still unknown. It has attracted the attention of cryptographers and historians alike. The manuscript remains one of the most intriguing mysteries in the history of writing.

    It witnessed the development of writing systems and the construction of monumental structures. The era came to an end with the collapse of many great civilisations. The Bronze Age laid the foundation for the rise of classical civilisations.

The history of writing is a long and fascinating journey from ancient pictograms to modern alphabets. The first writing systems, such as cuneiform and hieroglyphics, appeared around 3000 BC. Writing revolutionised the way societies recorded information and communicated.
    The invention of the alphabet by the Phoenicians was a significant step in making writing more accessible. This form of communication has shaped the evolution of human knowledge. Writing remains one of the most important inventions in the history of our species.

The first civilisation in the world arose in the Fertile Crescent, a region in the Middle East. The Sumerians, who lived in Mesopotamia, are considered the first to develop a complex society. They built cities, developed writing, and had a sophisticated legal system.
    The Sumerians are also known for their impressive ziggurats, monumental structures with religious significance. They laid the foundation for the civilisations that followed in the region. Their legacy in writing, mathematics, and architecture has influenced the world.

The history of the horse is deeply intertwined with human history. Horses were domesticated around 3000 BC and revolutionised transportation and agriculture. They played a vital role in warfare, exploration, and the development of societies.
    The horse became a symbol of power and freedom. Even today, horses are valued for their companionship and sport. Their importance to human progress is immeasurable.

The history of the potato is a story of globalisation and adaptation. Originating in South America, the potato was brought to Europe by Spanish explorers. It quickly became a staple crop, particularly in Ireland, due to its hardiness and nutritional value.
    The potato had a significant impact on agriculture and diet, contributing to population growth. It is now cultivated around the world. The potato's journey from the Andes to global importance is fascinating.

    Coffeehouses became centres of social and intellectual life in many countries. Coffee has become an integral part of daily life for millions of people. Its journey from ancient Ethiopia to global ubiquity is a remarkable story.

The first roads were built to facilitate trade and military movement. Early road systems were created by civilisations like the Romans and Persians. The Roman road network was particularly famous for its engineering and durability.
    Roads have been a key factor in the growth and spread of civilisations. They facilitate economic development and cultural exchange. The development of transport infrastructure is crucial to modern life.

The history of the guitar is long and varied. It likely originated from ancient string instruments in Central Asia and was brought to Europe by the Moors. The guitar evolved over time, from the early lute to the modern acoustic guitar.
    The guitar is now one of the most popular instruments in the world. It is used in a wide range of music genres, from classical to rock. Its versatility and accessibility have made it a beloved instrument.

The first known Olympic Games were held in ancient Greece in 776 BC. They were part of a religious festival in honour of Zeus. The games featured only one event, the stade footrace, which was about 600 feet long.
    The Olympic Games grew to include more events and became a major Panhellenic festival. They were revived in the modern era in 1896. The spirit of competition and international unity remains central to the modern Olympics.

The history of the calendar is a story of human attempts to measure time. Early calendars were based on lunar cycles and were used in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. The Roman calendar was later refined into the Julian calendar.
    The modern Gregorian calendar, which is now used internationally, is based on the solar year. The calendar is an essential tool for organising our lives and society. Its history is a testament to human ingenuity.

The history of the book is a narrative of the evolution of knowledge. From ancient scrolls to the modern printed page, the book has been a central vehicle for storing and transmitting information. The invention of paper in China greatly facilitated this process.
    The printing press revolutionised the production of books and made knowledge more accessible. Today, books continue to be a vital medium for education and entertainment. The book remains one of the most important inventions in human history.

The history of the wheel is one of the most important in human history. The wheel was first used around 3000 BC in Mesopotamia for pottery making. It revolutionised transportation and agriculture, enabling a wide range of new activities.
    The wheel is a fundamental invention that underpins many modern technologies. Its discovery was a major turning point in human civilisation. The wheel has been used for everything from chariots to modern cars.

    The violin has also been adopted in folk and jazz music. It is one of the most versatile and widely used instruments. Its history is a testament to the power of artistic expression.

The first known settlement is considered to be Jericho in the Jordan Valley. Jericho was inhabited as early as 9000 BC, making it one of the oldest continuous settlements. Its location near a spring made it favourable for agriculture.
    Jericho was characterised by a fortified wall and a tower, suggesting a degree of social organisation. The site provides important insights into early urban life. Jericho is a significant archaeological site for understanding the origins of civilisation.

The history of the silk road is a narrative of exchange and connection. It connected China, India, and the Middle East with Europe. It facilitated the trade of silk, spices, and other goods, and also the exchange of culture and ideas.
    The silk road was a conduit for the spread of technologies and religions. Its legacy continues to influence relations between these regions today. The silk road is a testament to the interconnectedness of our world.

The concept of the atom dates back to ancient Greece, with the philosopher Democritus proposing that all matter is made of indivisible particles. However, it was not until the 19th century that scientists began to develop a modern atomic theory.
    John Dalton's work in the early 19th century laid the foundation for modern chemistry. Experiments in the 20th century revealed the atom's subatomic structure. The study of the atom is central to understanding the nature of matter.

The history of the computer is a story of rapid technological progress. The first computers were mechanical, like the abacus, which was used for calculations. The development of electronic computers in the mid-20th century revolutionised computing.
    The invention of the microchip enabled computers to become smaller and more powerful. Computers are now fundamental to nearly every area of modern life. The history of computing reflects a unique period of technological advancement.

The first railway was a revolutionary development in transport. The Stockton and Darlington Railway in England, opened in 1825, was the first public railway to use steam locomotives. It marked the beginning of the railway age and transformed trade and travel.
    Railways enabled the rapid movement of goods and people over long distances. They contributed to the growth of industries and cities. Railways reshaped the landscape and economies of many countries.

The history of the camera is a journey of visual capture. The first cameras were large and used film, which had to be developed in a darkroom. The invention of digital cameras revolutionised photography, making it easier and more accessible.
    The camera has become ubiquitous in modern life, used in everything from phones to surveillance. It has transformed how we document our world and preserve memories. The camera is one of the most important inventions for capturing our history.

The history of the printing press is a narrative of democratising knowledge. Before its invention, books were rare and hand-copied. The printing press, developed by Gutenberg, allowed for mass production of books, making them widely accessible.
    The printing press is central to the spread of literacy and education. It played a key role in the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution. The printing press is one of the most important inventions in human history.

    Submarines can operate underwater for extended periods and are vital for strategic military operations. They are also used for research and exploration. The submarine is a fascinating example of engineering and military history.

    Telescopes have grown increasingly powerful, enabling us to see further into the cosmos. The invention of the telescope is one of the most significant in astronomy. It has fundamentally changed our view of the universe and our place within it.

    The compass played a crucial role in the Age of Discovery, enabling sailors to explore the world. It is still used in modern navigation, though often in conjunction with GPS. The compass is a symbol of orientation and discovery.

    The development of the pendulum clock and the wristwatch further refined time measurement. Clocks became essential for coordinating society and industry. The clock is an indispensable part of modern life.

    Aeroplanes have revolutionised travel, trade, and warfare. The ability to fly has brought the world closer together. The first flight is a testament to human innovation and determination.

    The periodic table is a fundamental tool for understanding the chemical world. It provides a framework for organising and predicting the behaviour of elements. The periodic table is one of the most important creations in the history of chemistry.

    Cars have transformed urban planning, industry, and daily life. The automobile is a symbol of independence and a major part of modern society. Its history reflects a century of technological progress.

    Radio has become an essential medium for news, music, and entertainment. It has shaped culture and politics. Radio is one of the most influential inventions in history.

    Television became a central source of information and entertainment in households worldwide. It has influenced culture and politics, shaping public opinion. The television is one of the most influential inventions of the modern era.
